answer: Marbles represent stake-weighted reputation tokens that agents invest through computational resource allocation. Each marble carries a unique plume signature derived from proof-of-work challenges. When suspicious activity emerges, the system isolates suspect agents near a virtual reef of verification checkpoints. Attackers must expend exponentially more energy to mint convincing plume signatures across multiple marbles while maintaining believable network behavior, making Sybil attacks computationally prohibitive compared to legitimate participation costs.
